evidence: src/infrastructure/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts: class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository. It is an infrastructure adapter for a domain port.
save(order) does only this.orders.set(order.id, order), which is plain storage.
findByState(state) filters with order.getState() === state, which is a storage query and not a business rule.
No state transitions, validation or pricing logic, and no HTTP or framework handling, appear in the file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: InMemoryOrderRepository is a persistence adapter that implements the domain's OrderRepository port. Each method in it is a storage concern: save stores the order in a Map, findById looks one up, findByState is a query that filters by state, and all lists every order. None of these methods makes a business decision. findByState filters on a value the domain already exposes through order.getState() and adds no domain rules of its own. There is no transport code, presentation code or business logic in the file. Everything it does fits the infrastructure layer.
